newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court delays hearing in Rao cheating case.
newsitem.headline: Indian court delays hearing in Rao cheating case.

text.p: A court on Wednesday delayed until next month a hearing in a criminal conspiracy case involving former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, the Press Trust of India said.
The news agency said district sessions judge Ajit Bharihoke set the hearing for November 6.

Rao had been scheduled to appear before Bharihoke on Wednesday to face charges of criminal conspiracy to cheat. But the judge said he was constrained by a Supreme Court ruling which exempts Rao from appearing in court until a lower court selects a more secure location than a crowded local tribunal.
Rao's lawyers convinced the Supreme Court last week that their client could be attacked by militant extremists if he appeared in one of the teeming local courts.
Rao has denied accusations that he helped defraud an expatriate businessman of $100,000 in 1983. The two other co-accused are in custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison, pending trial.
Rao has also been charged in a separate case of criminal forgery. A court hearing in that case had been scheduled for Monday, but was delayed until October 30.
Last week the former prime minister was granted bail in the seven-year-old forgery case after being briefly arrested at home, then immediately released. Rao has not commented publicly on the charges.
Rao stepped down as Congress party chief last month after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in the cheating case.
Rao's legal woes have shaken a tenuous political balance in the Indian capital.

Rao had pledged his Congress party's backing to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left minority coalition. But his successor, Sitaram Kesri, has threatened to withdraw the backing unless Deve Gowda backs a Congress alliance seeking to form the state government in Uttar Pradesh.
